accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the sequence of national income estimates released by the National Statistical Office?
o: First Advance Estimate → Second Advance Estimate → Provisional Estimate → First, Second and Third Revised Estimates
Second Advance Estimate → First Advance Estimate → Provisional Estimate → Revised Estimates
First Advance Estimate → Provisional Estimate → Second Advance Estimate → Revised Estimates
Provisional Estimate → First Advance Estimate → Second Advance Estimate → Revised Estimates
accepted.x: The prescribed sequence is First Advance Estimate, Second Advance Estimate, Provisional Estimate and thereafter First, Second and Third Revised Estimates.
accepted.tq: Arrange the estimate stages in sequence by identifying the provisional estimate as preceding the revised estimates.
accepted.sec: Release calendar - advance, provisional, revised estimates  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The First Advance Estimate of national income is generally released in:
o: The last working day of May of the following year
7 June of the same financial year
Early January of the same financial year
End-February of the following financial year
accepted.x: The First Advance Estimate is released in early January of the same financial year.
accepted.tq: Use the timing-specific direct-recall approach for release-calendar questions.
accepted.sec: Release calendar - advance, provisional, revised estimates  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Advance estimates of national income are prepared primarily by using the:
accepted.x: Advance estimates use the benchmark-indicator method, which projects the relevant aggregates using available indicators.
accepted.tq: Identify the distinctive methodology associated with advance estimates.
accepted.sec: Release calendar - advance, provisional, revised estimates  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Second Advance Estimate:
1. It is generally released at the end of February.
2. The FY26 Second Advance Estimate in the new series was 7.6%.
3. It is released after the Provisional Estimate.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Second Advance Estimate is released at the end of February and the FY26 estimate in the new series was 7.6%. It precedes, rather than follows, the Provisional Estimate.
accepted.tq: Reject the statement that reverses the normal release order.
accepted.sec: Release calendar - advance, provisional, revised estimates  [APPSC]

accepted.s: With effect from 2026, the date for release of the Provisional Estimate was shifted to:
accepted.x: The Provisional Estimate, earlier released on the last working day of May, was shifted to 7 June from 2026 after consultation with ACNAS.
accepted.tq: Test the changed date against the earlier release date.
accepted.sec: Release calendar - advance, provisional, revised estimates  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The change in the release date of the Provisional Estimate was made after consultation with the:
accepted.x: The change to 7 June was made after consultation with the Advisory Committee on National Accounts Statistics, referred to as ACNAS.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between similarly placed statistical abbreviations and identify the advisory body.
accepted.sec: Release calendar - advance, provisional, revised estimates  [APPSC]

accepted.s: In interpreting an estimate of AP livestock growth, which consideration is most important?
o: Only the initial advance estimate is relevant for all analytical purposes
Revised estimates never alter the sign of reported growth
The estimate stage must be specified because the reported growth may differ between AE and FRE
A provisional estimate is always identical to the First Revised Estimate
accepted.x: The estimate stage must always be quoted. AP livestock growth was reported as +4.79% at AE but -0.51% at FRE, showing that even the sign may change.
accepted.tq: Apply the estimate-stage principle to a numerical reporting situation.
accepted.sec: Release calendar - advance, provisional, revised estimates  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which department estimates Gross State Domestic Product in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation alone
Directorate of Economics and Statistics, Andhra Pradesh
accepted.x: The Directorate of Economics and Statistics, Andhra Pradesh, estimates GSDP for the State.
accepted.tq: Use the institutional-authority trap by identifying the agency responsible for State accounts.
accepted.sec: GSDP estimation - DES AP, sectors, advance estimates  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Directorate of Economics and Statistics, Andhra Pradesh, estimates GSDP in how many sectors?
accepted.x: DES Andhra Pradesh estimates GSDP in nine sectors.
accepted.tq: Recall the exact sectoral coverage rather than confusing it with institutional-sector classification.
accepted.sec: GSDP estimation - DES AP, sectors, advance estimates  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The First Advance Estimate of Andhra Pradesh GSDP for 2025-26 at current prices was:
accepted.x: The 2025-26 First Advance Estimate placed Andhra Pradesh GSDP at Rs 17.62 lakh crore at current prices.
accepted.tq: Test the reported current-price GSDP figure through direct numerical recall.
accepted.sec: GSDP estimation - DES AP, sectors, advance estimates  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding State-level national accounts:
1. The APSES base year is 2011-12.
2. MoSPI's uniform GSVA guideline moves States towards the 2022-23 base.
3. States are required to keep State accounts consistent with national accounts.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. APSES continues to use 2011-12, while the uniform guideline moves States towards 2022-23 and requires consistency with national accounts.
accepted.tq: Combine the existing State practice with the direction of methodological harmonisation.
accepted.sec: GSDP estimation - DES AP, sectors, advance estimates  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Under the 2011-12 national accounts series, the headline measure of value added was:
accepted.x: The 2011-12 series adopted GVA at basic prices as the headline measure.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between closely related national-accounting aggregates.
accepted.sec: Base year methodology - 2011-12 changes, 2022-23 changes, criticism  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The MCA-21 database was introduced in the 2011-12 series mainly to estimate the private corporate sector through the:
accepted.x: The MCA-21 company database represented an enterprise approach and partly replaced the earlier reliance on ASI for the relevant estimation.
accepted.tq: Link the database with the distinctive estimation approach it represents.
accepted.sec: Base year methodology - 2011-12 changes, 2022-23 changes, criticism  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following was a major criticism of the 2011-12 national accounts series?
o: It abandoned GVA as a measure of value added
It showed unusually high manufacturing growth that did not match physical indicators
It used only household survey data for manufacturing
It completely excluded the private corporate sector
accepted.x: The series was criticised for unusually high manufacturing growth that was inconsistent with physical indicators and for overestimating the private corporate sector.
accepted.tq: Find the correctly stated criticism among claims that reverse the methodological facts.
accepted.sec: Base year methodology - 2011-12 changes, 2022-23 changes, criticism  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the new data sources used in the 2022-23 national accounts series?
accepted.x: GST, PFMS and e-Vahan are specifically listed as new data sources for the 2022-23 series. MCA-21 continues to be used for organised manufacturing but is not included in this particular list of new data sources.
accepted.tq: Find the item that belongs to the continuing methodology rather than the listed new data sources.
accepted.sec: Base year methodology - 2011-12 changes, 2022-23 changes, criticism  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following methods was included in the 2022-23 series for extending estimates through quantity-based indicators?
accepted.x: Volume extrapolation was included among the methodological features of the 2022-23 series.
accepted.tq: Identify the precise technical term rather than a broad but incorrect estimation description.
accepted.sec: Base year methodology - 2011-12 changes, 2022-23 changes, criticism  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly states the revised growth figures for 2023-24 and 2024-25?
o: 2023-24 was revised from 9.2% to 7.2%, while 2024-25 was revised from 6.5% to 7.1%
2023-24 was revised from 7.2% to 9.2%, while 2024-25 was revised from 7.1% to 6.5%
Both years were revised downward by 2 percentage points
Both years were revised upward by 0.6 percentage points
accepted.x: The 2023-24 growth estimate was cut from 9.2% to 7.2%, whereas the 2024-25 estimate was raised from 6.5% to 7.1%.
accepted.tq: Compare the direction of revision separately for the two financial years.
accepted.sec: Base year methodology - 2011-12 changes, 2022-23 changes, criticism  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The nominal GDP estimate for 2022-23 in the revised series was:
accepted.x: Nominal GDP for 2022-23 was revised to Rs 261 lakh crore from the earlier Rs 269 lakh crore.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the revised value from the earlier estimate and from the 2025-26 figures.
accepted.sec: Base year methodology - 2011-12 changes, 2022-23 changes, criticism  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the nominal GDP estimates for 2025-26 before and after revision?
o: Rs 345 lakh crore to Rs 357 lakh crore
Rs 357 lakh crore to Rs 345 lakh crore
Rs 261 lakh crore to Rs 269 lakh crore
Rs 269 lakh crore to Rs 261 lakh crore
accepted.x: The nominal GDP estimate for 2025-26 was revised downward from Rs 357 lakh crore to Rs 345 lakh crore.
accepted.tq: Read the direction of revision carefully and separate 2025-26 from 2022-23 values.
accepted.sec: Base year methodology - 2011-12 changes, 2022-23 changes, criticism  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following sectoral revisions in the new series:
1. Agriculture was revised upward in the range of 3.8% to 5.9%.
2. Finance, real estate and dwellings were revised upward in the range of 7.8% to 9%.
3. Trade GVA was revised downward by 36%.
4. Road transport was revised downward by 16.9%.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four sectoral revisions are correctly stated: agriculture and finance-related activities were revised upward, while trade and road transport were revised downward.
accepted.tq: Check both the direction and the exact range or percentage for each sector.
accepted.sec: Base year methodology - 2011-12 changes, 2022-23 changes, criticism  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which statement regarding organised manufacturing and the unincorporated manufacturing sector is correct?
o: MCA-21 is used only for agriculture, and the unincorporated share is 7.8%.
MCA-21 continues to be used for organised manufacturing, while the unincorporated share of manufacturing GVA is 13.9%.
MCA-21 was discontinued, and the unincorporated share is 36%.
ASI alone is used for organised manufacturing, and the unincorporated share is 16.9%.
accepted.x: MCA-21 continues to be used for organised manufacturing, and the unincorporated sector accounts for 13.9% of manufacturing GVA.
accepted.tq: Pair the continuing database with the precise unincorporated-sector share.
accepted.sec: Base year methodology - 2011-12 changes, 2022-23 changes, criticism  [APPSC]

accepted.s: In 2011-12, the number of manufacturing companies listed in MCA was approximately:
accepted.x: The MCA database listed 1,35,802 manufacturing companies in 2011-12, compared with 67,649 corporate factories in ASI.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the company count in MCA from the factory count in ASI.
accepted.sec: Base year methodology - 2011-12 changes, 2022-23 changes, criticism  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following is the correct set of institutional sectors used in the 2022-23 national accounts series?
o: Government, public corporations, private corporations and households
Public corporations, agriculture, trade and households
Private corporations, industries, imports and government
accepted.x: The four institutional sectors are government, public corporations, private corporations and households.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure pair of public and private corporations and complete the institutional classification.
accepted.sec: Base year methodology - 2011-12 changes, 2022-23 changes, criticism  [APPSC]

accepted.s: What was done to data relating to periods before 2011-12 when the new methodology was introduced?
o: It was permanently excluded from national accounts
It was calculated exclusively from ASI data
It was replaced only by current-price estimates
It was recalculated using the new method as a back series
accepted.x: Data before 2011-12 were recalculated using the new methodology to construct a back series.
accepted.tq: Identify the treatment of historical data associated with a revised national accounts series.
accepted.sec: Base year methodology - 2011-12 changes, 2022-23 changes, criticism  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The manufacturing GVA figure of Rs 38.6 lakh crore, equivalent to 14.7% of GDP in 2023-24, was noted to be inconsistent with:
accepted.x: The reported manufacturing GVA of Rs 38.6 lakh crore did not match the totals obtained from ASI plus ASUSE.
accepted.tq: Link the reported discrepancy to the two statistical sources specifically identified with it.
accepted.sec: Base year methodology - 2011-12 changes, 2022-23 changes, criticism  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which statement about the Household Consumption Expenditure Survey is correct?
o: HCES was used only for estimating road transport GVA
HCES 2017-18 was the first full survey since 2011-12
HCES 2022-23 replaced the 2011-12 survey without any intervening survey results
HCES 2022-23 was the first full survey since 2011-12
accepted.x: HCES 2022-23 was the first full Household Consumption Expenditure Survey since 2011-12; the 2017-18 results were withheld.
accepted.tq: Use the chronology of surveys and distinguish conducted results from withheld results.
accepted.sec: Base year methodology - 2011-12 changes, 2022-23 changes, criticism  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Quarterly GDP estimates are generally released approximately:
o: On the last working day of May irrespective of the quarter
One year after the quarter ends
At the beginning of January of the same quarter
Two months after the quarter ends
accepted.x: Quarterly GDP estimates are released about two months after the relevant quarter ends, although older material had indicated about one month.
accepted.tq: Test the release lag while avoiding confusion with the annual estimate calendar.
accepted.sec: Quarterly GDP estimates - lag and data sources

accepted.s: Which of the following improves the estimation of quarterly GDP?
o: Only the final revised annual estimates
accepted.x: Quarterly estimates use high-frequency indicators, and GST data has further improved the information base.
accepted.tq: Identify the data source that is available at high frequency and suited to quarterly estimation.
accepted.sec: Quarterly GDP estimates - lag and data sources

accepted.s: The reported growth rate of GDP in the third quarter of FY26 was:
accepted.x: GDP growth in Q3 of FY26 was reported at 7.8%. The figures 7.6% and 7.4% relate to FY26 advance estimates, not Q3 growth.
accepted.tq: Separate a quarterly growth figure from annual advance-estimate figures.
accepted.sec: Quarterly GDP estimates - lag and data sources

accepted.s: Which of the following weaknesses in India's quarterly national accounts was flagged by the IMF?
o: Absence of a seasonally adjusted series and a lag in disaggregating capital formation
Excessive use of seasonally adjusted series and immediate capital disaggregation
Non-use of GST data and absence of all annual estimates
Exclusive dependence on population census data
accepted.x: The IMF flagged the absence of a seasonally adjusted series and a lag in disaggregating capital formation.
accepted.tq: Select the option containing both weaknesses rather than reversing the IMF's criticism.
accepted.sec: Quarterly GDP estimates - lag and data sources
